key_insight: Full-spectrum deep learning detected separator contact defects during copper laser welding, with LSTM achieving the highest reported separator F1-score of 0.99.
engineering_relevance: Spectroscopic monitoring could help identify separator contact that risks thermal damage and safety issues in lithium-ion battery manufacturing.
method: Investigated fiber core diameter, slit width, optical configuration, and integration time.
Trained LSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, and CNN+LSTM models on spectroscopic signals.
Compared characteristic wavelength bands with the full 232–1110 nm spectrum.
evidence_signal: Separator F1-scores were 0.87–0.88 using 350–450 and 650–750 nm bands, versus 0.91–0.99 using the full spectrum.
watch_item: The abstract does not report dataset size or external validation, leaving performance across production conditions uncertain.
paper_title: Detection of Separator Contact Defects Using Spectroscopic Signals and Deep Learning in Copper Laser Welding for Lithium-Ion Batteries
